w: Swamishri gave a message to a local TV channel about the glory and history of the Swaminarayan maha-mantra.

This evening Swamishri graced the Annual Day programme of the Chhatralaya. After a few mono-acting presentations, a multi-media presentation on the story of the Chhatralaya's progress and activities, since the last eleven years, a drama, 'God Save Me', depicted today's academic atmosphere with sarcasm.

Swamishri then blessed the assembly, saying, "Students do not want to study today. And when the exam paper is difficult they copy and create an agitation but this does not help them in gaining anything. Study means study! If students make efforts, take care and sincerely study in silence and concentration then no matter how hard the exam paper may be they would have nothing to worry about. In fact he wastes his time in addictions, creating strikes, commotion and indulges in worldly attraction. "A student should nourish noble feelings and ambitions that he wants to study well, pass with good marks, serve his parents and his country, please God and attain moksha."

Fifteen thousand devotees had gathered for the birth anniversary celebration of Shastriji Maharaj. The senior sadhus, Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, Pujya Kothari Swami, Pujya Dr Swami and Pujya Mahant, addressed the assembly.

Swamishri honoured Pujya Bhadresh Swami for attaining a Ph.D. Then Swamishri inaugurated several new BAPS publications in Gujarati and Hindi: Life and Work of Bhagwan Swaminarayan (Gujarati) by Sadhu Adarshjivandas; Eight Saint-Poets of Bhagwan Swaminarayan (Hindi) by Sadhu Adarshjivandas; Life and Work of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj (Hindi) by Sadhu Vivekpriyadas; Reflections on Swaminarayan Sampraday (Hindi) compiled by Sadhu Nishkamsevdas and an audio bhajan cassette ‘Nam Tera Sukhakari’. Finally in his blessings Swamishri said, “From his childhood Shastriji Maharaj built mandirs to establish the principle of Akshar and Purushottam, which was his mission on earth. The Kothari of Vartal, Gordhandas Kothari, saw the unique qualities in Shastriji Maharaj and desired that he stay with him so that he could teach him administration and later hand over his duties to him, but Shastriji Maharaj refused. Viharilalji Maharaj (Acharya) also felt that if Shastriji Maharaj stayed with him then he would be of great service. But Shastriji Maharaj had no inclination for that either. Then on meeting Bhagatji Maharaj he came to understand the philosophy of Akshar Purushottam.”

In the evening, while seated for his meal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was watching a memorial video of Yogiji Maharaj. In this video show linking scenes of Yogiji Maharaj to various kirtans, many scenes were repeated again and again.

Seeing the same scenes repeated, everyone present was talking among themselves when Swamishri spoke up: "Even if the same scenes come again and again, Jogi Bapa was such that however many times we have his darshan, we never get tired. There is only joy and joy. He was a carefree, blissful form."
This was a darshan of Swamishri's unique love for his guru.

In Indian politics today a bad practice prevails: even when the ruling party makes good plans, the opposition opposes them and does not let the work happen. Because of this, both the people's money and the country's development are held up. Pained by this, Pramukh Swami Maharaj spoke today in a certain context and said, "Opposition is a good thing. If there is opposition, people stay alert, so an opposition party is necessary. But to oppose in every matter (even in good matters)! When something good is happening for the people, one should support it, shouldn't one! But nobody understands this."

ds.t: Support what is good for the people
w: In Indian politics today a bad habit prevails: even when the ruling party makes good plans, the opposition opposes them and stops the work. Because of this, both the people's money and the nation's development are held up. Troubled by this, Swamishri said today while speaking about it, "Opposition is a good thing. With opposition people stay alert, so an opposition party is needed. But to oppose everything (even good things)! When it is for the people's good, one should give support, shouldn't one! But no one understands that."

st.t: British MP Bob Blackman Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi
w: British MP Robert John Blackman, better known as Bob Blackman, from Harrow East in the UK along with spouse Mrs. Nicola Blackman visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to experience India’s ageless beauty, borderless culture and timeless values. Both Bob and Nicola Blackman are regular visitors to the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in London, which they have been supporting for more than the last 20 years.

On behalf of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj – the inspirer & creator of Swaminarayan Akshardham and Spiritual Head of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha – senior sadhus traditionally welcomed Mr. Blackman with a garland of flowers, chandlo (vermillion powder) and the tying of the sacred kalva (sacred thread).
After admiring the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate), the Blackmans made their way to the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir where they witnessed the world’s ‘Largest Comprehensive Hindu Temple’.

After offering respects and viewing the mandir’s architecture, the Blackmans visited the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth) that includes 148 life-sized carved stone elephants depicting message of social harmony, peace and spirituality.

The Blackmans offered prayers for world peace and harmony by offering ‘abhishek’, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India on the sacred image of Sri Neelkanth Varni

Thereafter the British MP and his spouse experienced the educational exhibitions: Sahajanand Darshan (Hall of Values) – robotic shows depicting the ideals of nonviolence, honest, harmony and faith, Neelkanth Darshan – a Giant Screen film on the epic journey of Neelkanth Varni throughout India and Sanskruti Vihar – a cultural voyage that sails through 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage, highlighting India’s contributions to humanity through the ages. Finally, they witnessed the Sahaj Anand Water Show , a theatrical presentation about an ancient Upanishad story with modern fountains, projections, lasers and fire.

Sharing his experience at Akshardham, British MP Bob Blackman wrote, “Thank you for a wonderful experience. This is truly one of the wonders of the world, combing the lessons of history with modern technology. I have been privileged to be involved in the development of the Neasden Temple in the UK. This experience surpasses even the wonders of the Neasden Temple. I am proud to be an Honorary Hindu and this is truly an amazing dedication of voluntary effort to create this magnificent mandir. ”

Mahant Swami Maharaj sat in his room for breakfast. Gnanratnadas Swami, telling of the special antics of former students during their stay at the hostel, said, "All sorts of youths like this come to the hostel."
Swamishri said, "Even so, they are muktas (liberated souls)."
Those whom we see as mischief makers, Swamishri sees as muktas of Akshardham. What a contrast!
